title: Police Seek Suspect in $9 Million Gold Bar Scam on Upper West Side
meta_title: Police Seek Suspect in $9 Million Gold Bar Scam on Upper West Side
meta_description: The NYPD is searching for a suspect who stole $9 million in gold bars from a 67-year-old victim targeted in an elaborate online fraud scheme.
discover_titles: NYPD Seeks Suspect in $9 Million Gold Bar Heist
How a 67-Year-Old Fell Victim to a $9M Gold Scam
Police Release Footage of $9M Upper West Side Gold Theft
spot: More than a year and a half after a 67-year-old New Yorker handed over $9 million in gold bars to a fraudster on the Upper West Side, the New York Police Department has released security footage asking for the public's help to identify the suspect.
content_html:
Key Developments

The New York Police Department is asking for the public's assistance in identifying a man who allegedly stole $9 million in gold bars in broad daylight. The incident took place on a Wednesday in April 2025 near 81st Street and Broadway on Manhattan's Upper West Side.

According to authorities, a 67-year-old New Yorker became the target of an online fraud scheme after receiving a deceptive alert on his computer indicating his financial assets were compromised. Believing he needed to secure his funds, the victim purchased approximately 69 one-kilogram gold bars—each roughly the size of a chocolate bar—and brought them to an arranged meeting point. When he handed over the heavy sack, the suspect fled on foot.

Investigators recently released security camera footage and images of the suspect connected to the grand larceny investigation. Industry experts, including Isaac Kahan, owner of Bullion Trading LLC in Manhattan’s Diamond District, expressed astonishment at the physical logistics of the theft, noting that 69 one-kilo bars weigh well over 150 pounds.

Key Takeaways

  • The Heist: A 67-year-old victim handed over a bag containing $9 million in gold bars to a fraudster on the Upper West Side in April 2025.
  • The Scheme: The victim acted on instructions from an online scam after a fake computer alert led him to believe his financial assets were compromised.
  • Police Appeal: Over a year and a half after the incident, the NYPD has released security camera footage to identify the fleeing suspect.

Why It Matters

This high-value fraud highlights an increasingly common and sophisticated type of financial scam targeting older adults, often leveraging urgency and fear regarding compromised digital assets. Precious metals dealers note that fraudsters routinely persuade vulnerable victims to liquidate traditional retirement and bank accounts to purchase physical gold bars, exploiting a medium that offers anonymity and makes recovery exceptionally difficult for law enforcement.
